# Homework 3

Develop working knowledge of linear models in R: fitting them, reading diagnostic plots, and judging when a model is (or is not) correctly specified.

## Part A: Simulation Foundation

### Question 1

``` {r, eval=TRUE, show=TRUE}
set.seed(1234)
x <- 1:20
y <- 20+10*1:20+5*(1:20)^2+rnorm(20,0,200)

df <- data.frame(
  X = x,
  Y = y
)

lm.intOnly <- lm(Y~1, data=df)
lm.linear <- lm(Y ~ X, data=df)
lm.para <- lm(Y ~ X + I(X^2), data=df)

intOnly.pred <- predict(lm.intOnly)
linear.pred <- predict(lm.linear)
para.pred <- predict(lm.para)

intOnly.resid <- residuals(lm.intOnly)
linear.resid <- residuals(lm.linear)
para.resid <- residuals(lm.para)

plot(intOnly.pred, intOnly.resid, xlab="Fitted", ylab="Residual", main="Intercept only Residual vs Fitted")
abline(h=0,lty=2)
plot(intOnly.pred, df$Y, xlab="Predicted", ylab="Observed", main="Intercept only predicted vs observered")
abline(0,1,lty=2)
```

The model created by fitting Y observations to only the intercept does not produce a very good model. We can determine this by observing the lack of fit to the Predicted:Observed dashed line in the predicted vs observed plot. 

``` {r, eval=TRUE, show=TRUE}
plot(linear.pred, linear.resid, xlab="Fitted", ylab="Residual", main="Y ~ X Residual vs Fitted")
abline(h=0,lty=2)
plot(linear.pred, df$Y, xlab="Predicted", ylab="Observed", main="X~Y predicted vs observered")
abline(0,1,lty=2)
```

In the model created by fitting Y observations to X, we get a much better model compared to just fitting to intercept. As we can observe, the observed vs predicted plots fall closer to the y=x diagonal line compared to before.

``` {r, eval=TRUE, show=TRUE}
plot(para.pred, para.resid, xlab="Fitted", ylab="Residual", main="Y ~ X + I(X^2) Residual vs Fitted")
abline(h=0,lty=2)
plot(para.pred, df$Y, xlab="Predicted", ylab="Observed", main="X + I(X^2) predicted vs observered")
abline(0,1,lty=2)

A <- coef(lm.para)["I(X^2)"]
B <- coef(lm.para)["X"]
C <- coef(lm.para)["(Intercept)"]
```

In this final model, we fit Y to a parametric model, and we should expect best fit here since we know the Y variable was created dependent of X in a polynomial relationship. When we observe the predicted vs observed plot here we can see even better grouping of points near the y=x diagonal. The true coefficients of the function AX^2+BX+C is, A = 5 B = 10 and C = 20. In the model fitted above we observed coefficients of A = `r A`, B=`r B`, and C=`r C`. As we can see the noise that we introduced by adding 200 normally distributed points of mean 20 and sd 200 altered the coefficients from their "True" values. 

## Part B: Applying to real world data

Let's download some gene expression data from GEO. 
``` {r}
GEODataDownload <- function(DS, gpl, gsm, PlateAnnotInfo, GenerateMetaData, Technology, CountsFile = NULL){
  library(DESeq2); library(limma); library(data.table)
  if(Technology == "Array"){
    gset <- getGEO(DS, GSEMatrix = TRUE, getGPL = FALSE)
    if(length(gset) == 1) {
      idx <- 1
    } else {
      idx <- grep(gpl, attr(gset, "names"))
    }
    
    if(length(idx) != 1) {
      stop("Could not uniquely identify the requested GPL platform.")
    }
    
    gset <- gset[[idx]]
    print(gset)
    ex <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(gset)
    Pdat <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(gset))
    print(Pdat)
    comp <- gsub(" ", "", gsm)
    comp <- gsub(",", "", comp)
    gsms <- paste0(comp)
    #### Set up raw names ####
    sml <- c()
    for(i in 1:nchar(gsms)){ sml[i] <- substr(gsms,i,i)}
    qx <- as.numeric(quantile(ex, c(0., 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.99, 1.0), na.rm=T))
    LogC <- (qx[5] > 100) ||
      (qx[6]-qx[1] > 50 && qx[2] > 0) ||
      (qx[2] > 0 && qx[2] < 1 && qx[4] < 2)
    if(LogC){ ex[which(ex <= 0)] <- NaN
    ex <- log2(ex) }
    print(ex)
    sml <- paste("G", sml, sep="")
    f1 <- as.factor(sml)
    design <- model.matrix(~f1 + 0)
    colnames(design) <- levels(f1)
    fit <- lmFit(ex, design)
    cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(G1-G0, levels = design)
    fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont.matrix)
    fit2 <- eBayes(fit2, 0.01)
    tT <- topTable(fit2, adjust="fdr", sort.by = "B", number = 25000000000)
    #### subset ####
    tT$ID <- rownames(tT)
    ex2 <- data.table(subset(tT, select=c("ID", "logFC", "P.Value", "adj.P.Val")))
    ex2$ID <- as.character(ex2$ID)
    #### annotate with gene names ####
    plat <- PlateAnnotInfo[GPLID == gpl,][,!"GPLID", with = FALSE]
    if(nrow(plat) == 0){ print(paste("There is no annotation information available for", gpl)) }
    plat$ID <- as.character(plat$ID)
    plat <- plat[!duplicated(plat$ID),]
    ex2 <- merge(plat, ex2, by = "ID")
    ex2$ID <- as.character(ex2$ID)
    exraw <- data.table(ex)
    exraw$ID <- as.character(rownames(ex))
    #### annotate raw data with gene names ####
    ex2 <- merge(ex2, exraw, by = "ID")
    #### Generate Meta Data ####
    #### Add Meta data ####
    return(list(Data = ex2, MetaData = Pdat))
  }
  
  if(Technology == "RNAseq"){
    ACC <- paste("acc=", DS, sep = "")
    file <- paste("file=", DS, "_raw_counts_GRCh38.p13_NCBI.tsv.gz", sep = "")
    comp <- gsub(" ", "", gsm)
    comp <- gsub(",", "", comp)
    gsms <- paste0(comp)
    #### Set up DEG names ####
    urld <- "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/download/?format=file&type=rnaseq_counts"
    path <- paste(urld, ACC, file, sep="&");
    if(is.null(CountsFile)) CountsFile <- path
    cts <- data.table::fread(CountsFile, header=T)
    tbl <- as.matrix(cts, rownames="GeneID")
    exraw <- tbl
    #### Gene annotation from AnnotationHub (GEO GeneIDs are NCBI Entrez IDs) ####
    library(AnnotationHub)
    ah <- AnnotationHub()
    orgdbs <- query(ah, c("OrgDb", "Homo sapiens"))
    orgdb <- orgdbs[[tail(names(orgdbs), 1)]]
    annot <- suppressMessages(AnnotationDbi::select(orgdb, keys = rownames(tbl), keytype = "ENTREZID", columns = c("SYMBOL", "GENENAME")))
    annot <- annot[!duplicated(annot$ENTREZID), ]
    annot <- data.frame(GeneID = as.integer(annot$ENTREZID), Symbol = annot$SYMBOL, Description = annot$GENENAME)
    rownames(annot) <- annot$GeneID
    sml <- strsplit(gsms, split="")[[1]]
    sel <- which(sml != "X")
    sml <- sml[sel]
    tbl <- tbl[ ,sel]
    gs <- factor(sml)
    groups <- make.names(c("Ctrl", "Tx"))
    levels(gs) <- groups
    sample_info <- data.frame(Group = gs, row.names = colnames(tbl))
    keep <- rowSums( tbl >= 10 ) >= min(table(gs))
    tbl <- tbl[keep, ]
    ds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData=tbl, colData=sample_info, design= ~Group)
    ds <- DESeq(ds, test="Wald", sfType="poscount")
    r <- results(ds, contrast=c("Group", groups[2], groups[1]), alpha=0.05, pAdjustMethod ="fdr")
    tT <- r[order(r$padj)[1:length(r$padj)],]
    tT <- merge(as.data.frame(tT), annot, by=0, sort=F)
    tT <- subset(tT, select=c("GeneID","padj","pvalue","lfcSE","stat","log2FoldChange","baseMean","Symbol","Description"))
    #### subset ####
    ex2 <- data.table(subset(tT, select=c("GeneID", "Symbol", "Description", "log2FoldChange", "pvalue", "padj")))
    #### Adjust column names ####
    setnames(ex2, c("GeneID", "Symbol", "Description"), c("ENTREZID", "SYMBOL", "GENENAME"))
    #### Get Raw data ####
    GeneID <- as.integer(rownames(exraw))
    exraw <- as.data.table(exraw)
    #### Update column names ####
    exraw$ENTREZID <- GeneID
    #### merge FC and raw data together ####
    mer <- merge(ex2, exraw, by = "ENTREZID")
    return(mer)
  }
}

}

effectAnalysis <- function(summarizedExperiment, gene, metadata, colData = FALSE, additional = FALSE, assayNum){
  # Filter the summarized experiment based on metadata variable
  if(colData){
    
    metadata <- t(colData(summarizedExperiment)[[metadata]])
  }else{
    metadata <- t(rowData(summarizedExperiment)[[metadata]])
    metadata <- t(metadata)
  }
  #Check the type of data that metadata is
  metadataType <- is.numeric(metadata)
  
  if (metadataType){
  #Collect the expression data for the selected gene
  expressionData <- assay(summarizedExperiment,assayNum)
  expressionData <- as.data.frame(expressionData)
  expressionData$Gene <- rowData(summarizedExperiment)$SYMBOL
  expressionData <- expressionData[,c("Gene", setdiff(names(expressionData), "Gene"))]
  
  index <- match(gene, rowData(summarizedExperiment)$SYMBOL)
  
  expressionData <- expressionData[index,]
  
  if (!colData){
    metadata <- metadata[index,]
  }
  
  expressionData <- expressionData[,-1]
  
  # Check if the dimensions are the same so that they can be tested against one another.
  equal <- identical(dim(expressionData), dim(metadata))
  
  #Transform the objects into numerical vectors for correlation test
  
  expressionData <- as.numeric(expressionData)
  metadata <- as.numeric(metadata)
  
  #Proceed with analysis if the dimensions are the same
  if (equal){
  
  model <- lm(metadata ~ expressionData)
  pVal <- anova(model)$"Pr(>F)"[1]
  if (additional){
    plot(model)
    print(summary(model))
    print(anova(model))
  }
  return(pVal)
  } else{
    print("The dimensions are not similar.")
  }
  }
}

beyondLinear <- function(summarizedExperiment, gene, metadata, colData = FALSE, method, dataOnly = FALSE, assayNum){
  # Filter the summarized experiment based on metadata variable
  metadataName <- metadata
  if(colData){
    
    metadata <- t(colData(summarizedExperiment)[[metadata]])
  }else{
    metadata <- t(rowData(summarizedExperiment)[[metadata]])
    metadata <- t(metadata)
  }
  #Check the type of data that metadata is
  metadataType <- is.numeric(metadata)
  
  if (metadataType){
  #Collect the expression data for the selected gene
  expressionData <- assay(summarizedExperiment,assayNum)
  expressionData <- as.data.frame(expressionData)
  expressionData$Gene <- rowData(summarizedExperiment)$SYMBOL
  expressionData <- expressionData[,c("Gene", setdiff(names(expressionData), "Gene"))]
  
  index <- match(gene, rowData(summarizedExperiment)$SYMBOL)
  
  expressionData <- expressionData[index,]
  
  if (!colData){
    metadata <- metadata[index,]
  }
  
  expressionData <- expressionData[,-1]
  
  # Check if the dimensions are the same so that they can be tested against one another.
  equal <- identical(dim(expressionData), dim(metadata))
  
  #Transform the objects into numerical vectors for correlation test
  
  expressionData <- as.numeric(expressionData)
  metadata <- as.numeric(metadata)
  
  #Proceed with analysis if the dimensions are the same
  if (equal){
  
  model <- lm(metadata ~ expressionData)
  pVal <- anova(model)$"Pr(>F)"[1]
  if (dataOnly){
    return(list(expressionData = expressionData, metadata = metadata))
  }else{
  if (method == "LOESS"){
    model <- loess(metadata ~ expressionData, sp=0.5)
      
    
  }else if (method == "GAM"){
    model <- gam(metadata ~ s(expressionData), method="REML")
  }else if (method =="linear"){
    model <- lm(metadata ~ expressionData)
  }
  else{
    print(paste("Method:",method," not recognized. Try again."))
  }
  return(model)
  }} else{
    print("The dimensions are not similar.")
  }
  }
}
```

### Question 2

``` {r, eval=TRUE, show=TRUE, cache=TRUE}
genes <- rowData(experiment)$SYMBOL
pValues <- numeric(length(genes))

for (gene in 1:length(genes)){
  
  pValues[gene] <- effectAnalysis(experiment, genes[gene], "AGE", colData = TRUE, additional = FALSE, assayNum = 1)
}
```

``` {r, eval=TRUE, show=TRUE}
hist(pValues)

mostSig.index <- which.min(pValues)
mostSig <- genes[mostSig.index]

leastSig.index <- which.max(pValues)
leastSig <- genes[leastSig.index]
```

The gene that showed most significant relationship with age is, `r mostSig`.

``` {r, eval=TRUE,show=TRUE}
effectAnalysis(experiment, mostSig,"AGE",colData = TRUE, additional = TRUE, assayNum = 1)
```

The gene that showed the least significant relationship with age is, `r leastSig`

``` {r, eval=TRUE,show=TRUE}
effectAnalysis(experiment, leastSig,"AGE",colData = TRUE, additional = TRUE, assayNum = 1)
```

### Question 3

``` {r, eval=TRUE, show=TRUE}

geneData <- beyondLinear(experiment, mostSig, "AGE", colData = TRUE, method = "NA", dataOnly = TRUE, assayNum=1)
expressionData <- geneData$expressionData
metadata <- geneData$metadata

expData.4.pred <- seq(min(expressionData), max(expressionData), length.out=200)
newdata <- data.frame(expressionData=expData.4.pred)
LOESS.model <- beyondLinear(experiment, mostSig, "AGE", colData = TRUE, method = "LOESS", assayNum=1)
GAM.model <- beyondLinear(experiment, mostSig, "AGE", colData = TRUE, method = "GAM", assayNum=1)
linear.model <- beyondLinear(experiment, mostSig, "AGE", colData = TRUE, method = "linear", assayNum=1)

pred.LOESS <- predict(LOESS.model, newdata=newdata)
pred.GAM <- predict(GAM.model, newdata=newdata)
pred.linear <- predict(linear.model, newdata=newdata)
plot(expressionData, metadata, xlab=paste(mostSig, "Expression"), ylab="AGE", main=paste(mostSig, "Expression vs AGE"))

lines(expData.4.pred,pred.LOESS, col="steelblue", lwd=2)
lines(expData.4.pred,pred.GAM, col="tomato", lwd=2)
lines(expData.4.pred, pred.linear, col="magenta", lwd=2)
legend("bottomright",
       legend=c("LOESS","GAM","Linear"),
       col=c("steelblue","tomato","magenta"),
       pch = NA,
       lty=1)
```

Calculate AIC:
``` {r, eval=TRUE, show=TRUE}
lm.aic <- AIC(linear.model)
#LOESS.aic <- AIC(LOESS.model)
GAM.aic <- AIC(GAM.model)
delta.AIC <- lm.aic - GAM.aic
```

From the analysis above, we computed the AIC for the linear model (`r lm.aic`) and the GAM model (`r GAM.aic`). The difference in these two AIC values is `r delta.AIC`, thus we can determine the GAM plot is not any better than the linear plot as the difference is not greater than 2. 

```{r, eval=TRUE, show=TRUE}
resid.LOESS <- resid(LOESS.model)
resid.linear <- resid(linear.model)
resid.GAM <- resid(GAM.model)

enp.LOESS <- LOESS.model$enp
edf.GAM <- GAM.model$edf

n.LOESS <- length(resid.LOESS)
n.lm <- length(resid.linear)
n.GAM <- length(resid.GAM)


rss <- sum(resid.LOESS^2)
LOESS.aic <- n.LOESS*log(rss/n.LOESS)*(enp.LOESS+1)

aic_lm <- n.lm * log(sum(resid.linear^2) / n.lm) + 2 * (length(coef(linear.model)) + 1)
aic_gam <- n.GAM * log(sum(resid.GAM^2) / n.GAM) + 2 * (sum(edf.GAM) + 1)

delta.AIC.manual <- aic_lm - aic_gam
```

By calculating the values by hand we get the following AIC values; Linear: `r aic_lm`, GAM: `r aic_gam`, LOESS: `r LOESS.aic`. Here we see a similar relationship to above where the difference between linear and GAM models are below 2, indicating GAM is not any better than linear `r delta.AIC.manual`. This indicates that the linear model did not miss any relationship, and the non-linear models, GAM and LOESS, do not reveal more information regarding the relationship between `r mostSig` and AGE.

```{r, eval=TRUE, show=TRUE}
boxplot(list("Pre-Normalization"=as.vector(rawExp.mostSig),"Post-Normalization"=as.vector(normExp.mostSig)), ylab="Counts", main=paste("Boxplot of gene:", mostSig, "before and after normalization"))

```

```{r, eval=TRUE, show=TRUE, cache=TRUE}
pValues.norm <- numeric(length(genes))

for (gene in 1:length(genes)){
  
  pValues.norm[gene] <- effectAnalysis(experiment, genes[gene], "AGE", colData = TRUE, additional = FALSE, assayNum = 2)
}
```

```{r, eval=TRUE,show=TRUE}
hist(pValues.norm)

effectAnalysis(experiment, mostSig,"AGE",colData = TRUE, additional = TRUE, assayNum = 2)
```

In the box-plot of pre- and post- normalized RNAseq expression counts, it is observed that the boxplots do not appear different. The mean, IQR, and outlines appear similar. However, when we plot the distribution of p-values of the normalized data, we see that the p-value distributions are shifted left compared to the initial histogram of p-value distributions. Comparing the results of models produced with raw and normalized expression data for gene `r mostSig`. It appears that the residuals vs fitted plot has a fit closer to horizontal line 0, in the raw expression model, however the model created with normalized data has a lower p-value from ANOVA. 

However, in the individual boxplot of gene `r mostSig`, we can see that the variance is decreased after normalization. This reduction in variance can lead to more trustworthy results. 

``` {r, eval=TRUE, show=TRUE}
hist(pValues.norm)

mostSig.index.norm <- which.min(pValues.norm)
mostSig.norm <- genes[mostSig.index.norm]

leastSig.index.norm <- which.max(pValues.norm)
leastSig.norm <- genes[leastSig.index.norm]
```

The gene that showed most significant relationship with age, when model prepared with normalized data, is: `r mostSig.norm`.

``` {r, eval=TRUE,show=TRUE}
effectAnalysis(experiment, mostSig.norm,"AGE",colData = TRUE, additional = TRUE, assayNum = 2)
```

The gene that showed the least significant relationship with age, when model prepared with normalized data, is: `r leastSig.norm`

``` {r, eval=TRUE,show=TRUE}
effectAnalysis(experiment, leastSig.norm,"AGE",colData = TRUE, additional = TRUE, assayNum = 2)
```


### Question 5

```{r, eval=TRUE, show=TRUE}
mostSig.index.norm <- which.min(pValues.norm)
mostSig.norm <- genes[mostSig.index.norm]

geneData <- beyondLinear(experiment, mostSig, "AGE", colData = TRUE, method = "NA", dataOnly = TRUE, assayNum=2)
expressionData <- geneData$expressionData
metadata <- geneData$metadata

expData.4.pred <- seq(min(expressionData), max(expressionData), length.out=200)
newdata <- data.frame(expressionData=expData.4.pred)

LOESS.model <- beyondLinear(experiment, mostSig.norm, "AGE", colData = TRUE, method = "LOESS", assayNum=2)
GAM.model <- beyondLinear(experiment, mostSig.norm, "AGE", colData = TRUE, method = "GAM", assayNum=2)
linear.model <- beyondLinear(experiment, mostSig.norm, "AGE", colData = TRUE, method = "linear", assayNum=2)

pred.LOESS <- predict(LOESS.model, newdata=newdata)
pred.GAM <- predict(GAM.model, newdata=newdata)
pred.linear <- predict(linear.model, newdata=newdata)
plot(expressionData, metadata, xlab=paste(mostSig, "Expression"), ylab="AGE", main=paste(mostSig.norm, "Expression vs AGE"))

lines(expData.4.pred,pred.LOESS, col="steelblue", lwd=2)
lines(expData.4.pred,pred.GAM, col="tomato", lwd=2)
lines(expData.4.pred, pred.linear, col="magenta", lwd=2)
legend("bottomright",
       legend=c("LOESS","GAM","Linear"),
       col=c("steelblue","tomato","magenta"),
       pch = NA,
       lty=1)

lm.aic <- AIC(linear.model)
#LOESS.aic <- AIC(LOESS.model)
GAM.aic <- AIC(GAM.model)

print(lm.aic)
print(GAM.aic)
```

From the visual plot, the "GAM" model follows the data the best. When we evaluate the AIC for the linear and GAM plot, we can see that the GAM model (`r GAM.aic`) has a lower AIC than linear (`r lm.aic`). However, the difference is small, I will perform the rest of the evaluation with the linear model. 

```{r, eval=TRUE, show=TRUE}
pred.linear <- predict(linear.model)
plot(pred.linear, expressionData, xlab="Predicted", ylab="Observed", main="Predicted vs Observed for linear model \n modeled from normalized data")
abline(0,1,lty=2)

resid.linear <- resid(linear.model)
fitted.linear <- fitted(linear.model)

plot(fitted.linear, resid.linear, xlab="Fitted",ylab="Residuals", main="Fitted vs Observed for linear model \n modeled from normalized data")
abline(h=0,lty=2)

normalityTest <- shapiro.test(resid.linear)
normalityTest.pval <- normalityTest$p.value
```

We can see from the results of the Shapiro-Wilks test indicate we fail to reject the null hypothesis that the residuals of the model are normally distributed (`r normalityTest.pval`). We can thus assume that the model was fitted with wrong assumptions.
